definitions.explanation: A test where answers are written on paper, as opposed to an oral or practical exam. Common in school entrance exams, certification tests, and employment screenings in Japan.

examples.japanese: {筆記試験|ひっきしけん}に{合格|ごうかく}した。
{面接|めんせつ}の{前|まえ}に{筆記試験|ひっきしけん}がある。
examples.english: There is a written exam before the interview.

examples.japanese: {運転免許|うんてんめんきょ}を{取|と}るには{筆記試験|ひっきしけん}と{実技試験|じつぎしけん}の{両方|りょうほう}に{受|う}からなければならない。
examples.english: To get a driver's license, you must pass both the written and practical exams.

notes:
Compound of {筆記|ひっき} (writing) + {試験|しけん} (exam). A test where answers are written by hand, as opposed to oral or practical exams.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {筆記試験|ひっきしけん}を{受|う}ける: to take a written exam
- {筆記試験|ひっきしけん}に{合格|ごうかく}する: to pass a written exam
- {筆記試験|ひっきしけん}に{落|お}ちる: to fail a written exam

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {面接|めんせつ}: interview
- {口述試験|こうじゅつしけん}: oral exam
- {実技試験|じつぎしけん}: practical exam

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, many hiring processes include a {筆記試験|ひっきしけん} covering general knowledge or aptitude (often the SPI test). {入学試験|にゅうがくしけん} (entrance exams) and {資格試験|しかくしけん} (certification tests) also typically have a written component.
